finding: The release's stated deliverable -- "the escalation needs a name that exists" -- is defeated at the two surfaces an agent actually reads, and §2 prices the change at one sentence: "This release adds `audit-converge-on` to that enum and maps the field to it." Counted against the tree, a sixth name falsifies nine sites, none named here and none covered by any §5 test. Code comments: `engine/escalation.go:14` ("The five decisions §5.2 closes `tp escalate --decision` over. Four name a user-only operation §5.1 fences off" -- the 4/1 split becomes 5/1), `:29` ("the closed set in the order §5.2 writes it" -- §5.2 writes five and this spec gives the sixth no position), `:39`, `:47`; tests: `engine/escalation_test.go:60` ("a decision outside the closed five") and `cli/escalate_test.go:158`, which loops the five literals explicitly; `fakerunner/cmd/tp-fake-runner/main.go:260` ("§5.2's closed five"). Agent-facing docs: `skills/tp/REFERENCE.md:347` and `skills/tp/SKILL.md:247` each enumerate the five names, and those are the bytes every agent loads every session -- an agent reading them files `--decision other`, which is precisely the outcome the enum entry exists to remove, so the release buys the name and leaves the agent unable to learn it. And `spec/0.35.0.md:428-429` is a SHIPPED spec closing the set over five, with §5.1's fenced-operation list needing the fifth entry too. None of the nine fails a test: `escalate_test.go:158` only asserts the five are accepted, so the sixth ships with every "five" intact and green. The asymmetry is the point -- the same section spends a paragraph enumerating `fenceWorkflowWrite`'s four call sites "because two enumerations of this list have already been short" and a paragraph measuring `review_converge_on` at 16+11+2 files "measured rather than implied", then asserts the cost of the half this release actually invents.
suggestion: Enumerate the enum's sites in §2 the way it already enumerates the fence's: name `engine/escalation.go:14,29,39,47`, `escalation_test.go:60`, `escalate_test.go:158`, `fakerunner/.../main.go:260`, `REFERENCE.md:347` and `SKILL.md:247`, and state that `spec/0.35.0.md` §5.1/§5.2 are amended rather than contradicted. Give §5 a test with a failing arm over the cardinality -- assert `len(engine.EscalationDecisions()) == 6` and that the hint string and both doc tables carry `audit-converge-on` -- since test 10 as written passes with all nine sites stale.

finding: §1's sizing paragraph is now false, and it is the first thing any agent reads to decide how much of this release to plan for. It says: "Two deliverables, and only the first is a no-op by default. §2 ships `audit_converge_on` ... and changes nothing for a project that does not set it. §3 changes `consecutive_clean` and `converged` for **any** project whose spec moves between rounds, opted in or not. An earlier draft of this paragraph claimed the whole release was behaviour-preserving; it is not, and §3 is why." §3 was cut this round and is now titled "What this release deliberately does not contain"; it changes nothing for anyone. So the release now HAS one deliverable, IS behaviour-preserving by default, and the paragraph explicitly contradicts the section it cites, whose first sentence is that the mechanism "is not in it now". The AX cost is not cosmetic: this paragraph is what a decomposer sizes the task list from and what an auditor sizes its migration/regression surface from, so it buys planning for an install-time behaviour change that does not exist, and it does so in the one paragraph written to prevent exactly that error.
suggestion: Rewrite §1's last paragraph to the release's actual shape: one deliverable, `audit_converge_on`, a no-op by default, whose content is the fence and the escalation name rather than any behaviour change. Delete the "an earlier draft claimed the whole release was behaviour-preserving; it is not" sentence -- it is now true and the correction is the error.

finding: Cutting §3's mechanism and inserting two tests renumbered two reference spaces at once, and four references were not carried, each costing a reader one wrong jump. (1) Non-Goal 4: "§3 adds a function rather than altering the shared one precisely so review's `--status` cannot move" -- §3 adds no function; the non-goal is now trivially true and its stated reason is gone. (2) The reversed-guard paragraph: "`assert.Len(t, e, 3, ...)`, which ... §3's reset touches" -- there is no reset, so the one sentence explaining why that assertion is named is void. (3) The same paragraph: "§5 test 12 pins all nine" -- §5 now has eleven tests and it is test 11. This was 'repaired' this round from "test 9" (also wrong) to "test 12" (also wrong), so the reference has now been wrong in three consecutive drafts. (4) §2.2: "§5 test 5 uses a legacy row" -- test 5 is "`warning` is advisory"; the legacy row is test 7 ("Unrecognised fails closed ... a legacy row supplies only (a)"). This was bumped 4→5 for the one test inserted at the top, but two tests were inserted above it, so an off-by-one repair was applied where the shift was two. Note the mechanism: §3 was reused as a top-level heading number for a section that now contains nothing, which is what silently broke every surviving "§3" reference.
suggestion: Fix all four (Non-Goal 4 loses its §3 clause, the guard paragraph loses "which §3's reset touches" and says test 11, §2.2 says test 7). Then stop numbering references into a list that renumbers: cite the tests by their bolded title ("§5's `Unrecognised fails closed`") the way §4 already cites `TestAuditGate_NoEscapeHatchFromTheGate` by name, since a title survives an insertion and an ordinal does not. tp's `broken-cross-ref` lint covers `§X.Y step N` only, so nothing in the gate catches either shape.

finding: Test 8's fixture was widened this round from a projection to the whole corpus, and the widening is ~1.4 MB of committed bytes that no assertion reads. Round 5 asked for "the `(status, severity)` pairs of v0.35.0's nine recorded rounds ... copied into `testdata/`"; round 6 asks for "The rows of v0.35.0's nine recorded rounds and v0.36.0's thirteen, copied into `testdata/`". Measured on the source files: those 22 rounds are 1,453,664 bytes and 3,046 rows (v0.35.0 805,180 B / 1,800 rows; v0.36.0 648,484 B / 1,246 rows), of which **133 are non-`PASS`**. Every predicate this release adds reads exactly two keys, `status` and `severity`, and the whole of §2.1's table is decided by the (round, severity) of those 133 rows -- `blocking` by their severities, `all` by whether a round has any non-`PASS` row at all. The other 2,913 rows contribute one bit each and the other eight keys per row (`notes`, `location`, `class`, `category`, `evidence_file`, `evidence_lines`, `item_id`, `role`) contribute nothing: 133 projected rows is a few KB, so the widening is roughly two orders of magnitude of permanent repository weight for zero assertion strength. It is also the more brittle fixture: pinning full rows pins fields no rule constrains, so an unrelated schema addition rewrites 1.4 MB of testdata.
suggestion: Restore round 5's projection and extend it to both cycles: commit the `(round_index, status, severity)` triples -- or, smaller still, the per-round non-`PASS` severity counts -- with the source commit cited, and say in test 8 that the fixture is a projection so a later reader does not 'complete' it back to full rows. If the full rows are wanted for some other reason, say what assertion needs them.

finding: Pressing round 5's `by_severity` finding with new evidence rather than repeating it, because the round-5 repair corrected the pin count six→four and left the argument's reach untouched. Two facts, both measured. (1) tp's own code has already decided that a relaxed convergence predicate needs one byte distinguishing "clean because empty" from "clean because discounted", and classified that byte as decision-critical: `review_record.go:212` and `review_status.go:103` both read "next_action and nonblocking_open are decision-critical and survive it [--compact]", and `review_record.go:225-227` states "the field's mere presence signals the accepted-open state". `--compact` is tp's strictest AX filter; surviving it is the strongest statement tp makes about a byte. This release copies review's relaxation and declines the byte review calls decision-critical, then bills the operator for it in prose ("reads the round files for what was suppressed") -- an unbounded manual NDJSON read, which is the exact cost P3 exists to remove. (2) The four pins §4 now counts do not reach the cheapest route. All four -- `spec/0.31.0.md` §8.4 and its test 18, `REFERENCE.md:634`, and `reviewconvergeon_clean_test.go:185-205` (`TestReviewNonBlockingOpen_AuditUnaffected`, verified: it asserts only that `audit --record` and `audit --status` never emit the key) -- are about `nonblocking_open` on `--record`/`--status`. **None touches `tp audit --merge`**, which the loop already runs on the same rows in the same round immediately before `--record`, and whose summary at `audit_merge.go:61-86` already loops those rows building `by_status` and `by_role` and already carries a `--compact`-stripped explanatory key (`overlap_report`, `:90-92`). A `by_severity` counter over non-`PASS` rows there is ~6 lines inside an existing loop, no new command, no new flag, no new config, no round-trip, and inverts zero of the four pins. My verdict, asked for plainly: it is in scope -- it is the smallest surface on which this release's only feature is observable at all, and "deferred" here means the release ships a mechanism whose effect no agent can see.
suggestion: Add to §2's scope: `tp audit --merge`'s summary gains `by_severity`, a count of non-`PASS` rows by severity (with the unrecognised bucket §2's fail-closed rule already defines), emitted only when a non-`PASS` row exists and omitted under `--compact` like `overlap_report`; add a §5 test whose killing mutation is a counter that includes `PASS` rows. If it is still to be declined, say so IN Non-Goal 6 and give a reason that reaches `--merge`, because the four-pin reason does not -- and then state what an agent is expected to do with `clean: true` under `blocking`.

finding: The round-5 repair to the doc surface named claims -- but a different set of claims from the ones this release falsifies, and the appearance of an enumerated doc scope now hides that the two live ones are still unnamed. §2 gained `REFERENCE.md:519-522`, `spec/0.31.0.md:41` and `REFERENCE.md:327-328`: all three are the five-layer precedence sweep, a pre-existing wrongness this release cleans up. Verified still present and still unnamed anywhere in the spec are the two sentences the release itself makes false, both in the file every agent loads every session: (1) `SKILL.md:152-153`, inside the v0.32.0 scope lesson -- "tp has no audit-side equivalent of `review_converge_on` yet" -- which shipping the field falsifies, and whose naive repair ("now it does") teaches every agent that `audit_converge_on` closes the scope divergence, which Non-Goal 1 says in terms it does not; (2) `SKILL.md:145` -- "`tp audit --record` counts every row whose `status` is not exactly `PASS` ... so parking a finding leaves the round's finding count, the role streak and `--status --check` exactly where they were" -- whose `--status --check` clause is false under `blocking` for a `warning` or `info` row. Meanwhile §2's cost paragraph still puts the docs in scope by filename ("both `skills/tp/REFERENCE.md` and `skills/tp/SKILL.md`") and §5 still has no test or acceptance over either file. A wrong sentence in SKILL.md is not documentation debt: it is one wrong decision per agent per session, which is the most expensive byte tp owns, and it is the only cost in this release that recurs without bound.
suggestion: Name the two claims where §2 names the precedence sites: `SKILL.md:152-157` must keep saying the scope divergence is open (per Non-Goal 1) while no longer saying no audit equivalent exists, and `SKILL.md:145`'s disposition sentence must qualify its `--status --check` clause with the resolved `audit_converge_on`. Give §5 an acceptance naming both line ranges, so the doc edit has a failing arm rather than a filename.

finding: §3 is 29 lines (150-178) of withdrawn-draft history in a 265-line file whose own header records deleting that exact class -- "The prose recording which drafts were withdrawn is gone with them: it had grown to 77 of the file's 306 lines, which is `spec/0.43.0.md` §2's repair-verbosity class measured on this file." §3 is a round-by-round table of three review rounds' finding slugs, a paragraph on why `IsLegacyRound` does not discriminate, and a paragraph on why a review round cannot make a decision -- and it closes by pointing at `spec/0.46.0.md` §8.4, "with the measurements", i.e. the durable record already exists elsewhere. Renumbering Non-Goals from §3 to §4 as a consequence also removes the dangling "§3" target.
